cards.explanation: The answer is False. The LORD says, “Judah will be besieged, as well as Jerusalem.” Nobody gets a seat on the sidelines here, friends. Both of them are in the thick of it.

The answer is that they will be severely injured. The LORD says, “all who would heave it away will be severely injured.” Lift with your knees, they always say. Doesn't help when the thing you're lifting is a whole city.

The answer is False. The LORD says, “I will keep a watchful eye on the house of Judah, but I will strike with blindness all the horses of the nations.” So the blindness goes to the nations' horses, and Judah gets the watchful eye. A panicked horse that can't see is going to make for a very long day for its rider.

The answer is because the LORD of Hosts is their God. The leaders say, “The people of Jerusalem are my strength, for the LORD of Hosts is their God.” That little word “for” is where the reason starts, friends.

The answer is that they will be consumed on the right and the left. The LORD says the clans of Judah “…will consume all the peoples around them on the right and on the left…” So the peoples around them are consumed, on both sides. Judah is the firepot in that woodpile.

The answer is True. The LORD says He will make the clans of Judah like a firepot in a woodpile, like a flaming torch among the sheaves. Then He says they “…will consume all the peoples around them on the right and on the left, while the people of Jerusalem remain secure there.” So Judah's clans are the firepot, and Jerusalem's people are the ones who stay secure.

The answer is so King David's family and Jerusalem won't outshine Judah. The LORD saves Judah's tents first “…so that the glory of the house of David and of the people of Jerusalem may not be greater than that of Judah.” Judah's tents come first, friends, and that's the reason the LORD gives.

The answer is True. The LORD says He will defend the people of Jerusalem “…so that the weakest among them will be like David…” David became king over Israel (2 Samuel 5:3). That's a big promise for the weakest, friends.
The answer is destroy. The LORD says, “So on that day I will set out to destroy all the nations that come against Jerusalem.” He's the one who sets out, friends. It's His own move.

The answer is a spirit of grace and prayer. The LORD says, “…I will pour out on the house of David and on the people of Jerusalem a spirit of grace and prayer…” Grace and prayer. That's a gift poured out on them.
The answer is mourn. The LORD says, “…they will look on Me, the One they have pierced. They will mourn for Him…” I think this one hurts, friends. They'll look at Him and the grief will be real.
The answer is True. The text says, “They will mourn for Him as one mourns for an only child…” That's a deep kind of grief, friends, and the verse says it just that way.

The answer is sin. The LORD says the fountain is opened “…to cleanse them from sin and impurity.” A fountain is for washing, and I know what a flour-covered apron needs. What this one washes away is sin and impurity.
The answer is False. The LORD says He will erase the names of the idols from the land, “…and they will no longer be remembered.” They get erased and forgotten, friends.

The answer is that he has spoken falsely in the name of the LORD. His father and mother say, “You shall not remain alive, because you have spoken falsely in the name of the LORD.” I'll say it once: this is a heavy part. The charge is about speaking falsely in the LORD's name.
The answer is True. On that day the prophet “…will not put on a hairy cloak in order to deceive.” So the cloak stays off, friends. The verse says he's ashamed of his vision.

The answer is that he says he's not a prophet but a servant who works the land. He says, “I am not a prophet; I work the land, for I was purchased as a servant in my youth.” That's how he describes himself, friends, with no big title. One short bio.

The answer is that he received them in the house of his friends. He says, “These are the wounds I received in the house of my friends.” I think that's a rough place to get hurt. The text doesn't say more than that.

The answer is scattered. The LORD of Hosts says, “Strike the Shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered…” Jesus quotes this line to His disciples (Matthew 26:31). It's a heavy moment, friends, and the text says scattered.

The answer is that He will refine them like silver and test them like gold. The LORD says, “This third I will bring through the fire; I will refine them like silver and test them like gold.” It's fire, friends, but He's the one bringing them through it. And He's not done with them after that.
The answer is True. The LORD says, “They will call on My name, and I will answer them.” They call, and He answers, friends. It's that plain.

The answer is “They are My people.” The LORD says, “I will say, ‘They are My people,’ and they will say, ‘The LORD is our God.’…” Notice that both sides speak. He names them His, and they name Him their God. I think that's a family kind of line.
